start.1.title: Add a channel
start.1.text: A mailbox, a chat or a web address: the place your messages go to.
start.2.title: Write a message

msg.subject: Subject
msg.vars: Variables, filled in when the message is sent. The last one counts the days left until its date.
help.timezone: The message goes out when it is this time in the chosen time zone, and keeps that hour when the clocks change.
help.repeat: A repeating message goes out again every day, week, month or year. You choose how often, on which days of the week, and when it stops.
msg.paused.note: Paused. It will not be sent until you resume it.
channels.empty: No channels yet. A channel is a place messages can be sent to: a mailbox, a chat, a URL.
channel.name: Name
channel.name.hint: Only you see this. For example “Work mail”.
channel.test.hint: A test uses the saved settings. Email channels send it to their own From address.
channel.delete.confirm: Delete this channel and its history?
channel.secret.saved: Saved. Leave empty to keep it.
type.smtp.help: Works with any mailbox that offers SMTP. Gmail and most other providers want an app password here, not your usual one.
type.resend.help: Sends through Resend. You need an API key and a verified domain for the From address.
type.telegram.help: Create a bot with @BotFather, write to it or add it to a group, then paste its token and the chat ID.
type.discord.help: In Discord: channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → copy the webhook URL.
type.slack.help: Paste an incoming webhook URL from your Slack app.
type.webhook.help: Makes an HTTP request to any URL. The message text becomes the request body.
guide.title: Step by step
guide.smtp.1: Find the SMTP server of your mail provider and type it into “{host}”. Gmail: smtp.gmail.com. Outlook: smtp-mail.outlook.com. Yahoo: smtp.mail.yahoo.com. iCloud: smtp.mail.me.com. Leave “{port}” at 587.
guide.smtp.3: Gmail, Yahoo and iCloud do not accept your usual password here. In the security settings of your mail account turn on two-step verification, create an “app password” there and paste it into “{password}”.
guide.smtp.4: Type the same address into “{from_email}” and save. Then open the channel and press “{test}”: a test letter should arrive in your own mailbox.
guide.resend.1: Create a free account at resend.com.
guide.resend.2: Open Domains there, add your domain and create the DNS records Resend shows you. Wait until the domain is marked as verified.
guide.resend.3: Open API Keys, create a key and paste it into “{api_key}”. It starts with re_.
guide.resend.4: “{from_email}” must be an address on the verified domain, for example hello@your-domain.com.
guide.telegram.1: In Telegram open the chat with @BotFather and send it /newbot. Choose a name for the bot. BotFather replies with a token: paste it into “{bot_token}”.
guide.telegram.2: Open your new bot and press Start. To post to a group or a channel, add the bot there instead; in a channel it has to be an administrator.
guide.telegram.3: “{chat_id}” says where to send. For yourself: write to @userinfobot and copy the number it answers with. For a public channel: its name with @, like @mychannel. Group IDs are negative numbers.
guide.telegram.4: Save, then open the channel and press “{test}”.
guide.discord.1: In Discord hover over the channel and click the gear (Edit Channel). You need the Manage Webhooks permission on that server.
guide.discord.2: Open Integrations → Webhooks and press New Webhook.
guide.discord.3: Press Copy Webhook URL and paste it into “{webhook_url}”.
guide.slack.1: Open api.slack.com/apps, press Create New App → From scratch and choose your workspace.
guide.slack.2: In the menu of the app open Incoming Webhooks and switch them on. Press Add New Webhook to Workspace, choose the channel and allow.
guide.slack.3: Copy the address that starts with https://hooks.slack.com/ and paste it into “{webhook_url}”.
guide.webhook.1: Paste the address that should receive the request into “{url}”. Copy it whole, with https:// at the start.
guide.webhook.2: The text of the message is sent as the body of the request, exactly as you wrote it. To send JSON, write JSON in the message and leave “{content_type}” as application/json.
guide.webhook.3: If the service asks for a key, add it under “{headers}”, one per line, for example Authorization: Bearer abc123.
field.headers.hint: One per line, for example: Authorization: Bearer abc123
settings.changed: Password changed. Other devices have been signed out.
settings.export.hint: A JSON file with your messages and channels. Passwords and tokens are not included.
settings.delete.hint: Deletes your account together with all its messages and channels. This cannot be undone.
err.network: Can't reach the server. Check your connection.
err.unauthorized: You have been signed out. Sign in again.
err.not_configured: The server is not set up yet.
err.too_many_attempts: Too many attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again.
err.password_too_short: The password needs at least 10 characters.
err.email_taken: There is already an account with this email. Sign in instead.
err.signups_closed: This Postdate is not taking new accounts.
err.invalid_email: That doesn't look like an email address. Check “{field}”.
err.invalid_url: That doesn't look like a web address. Check “{field}”.
err.invalid_headers: Write each header as Name: value, one per line.
err.smtp_port_25: Port 25 is blocked on Cloudflare. Use 587 or 465.
err.too_many_recipients: That is too many recipients. The limit is 50.
err.too_long: That is too long for this channel.
err.invalid_time: Check the date, time and time zone.
err.channel_in_use: This channel still has scheduled messages. Delete or move them first.
err.decrypt_failed: Saved channel settings can't be read. SECRET_KEY has probably changed.
err.busy: This message is being sent right now. Try again in a moment.
err.not_found: That page or item doesn't exist.
